plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since the price I pay is determined by the second-highest bid (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value of $22 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest competing bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win against a high second bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $15, I will bid $15 to maximize expected profit, letting the auction mechanism naturally determine my payment based on competitors' bids.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay (I'd never win at a price above my value). Bidding higher risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $10, so I'll bid exactly that.
